COMPANY OVERVIEW
KKR is a leading global investment firm that offers alternative asset management as well as capital markets and insurance solutions. KKR aims to generate attractive investment returns by following a patient and disciplined investment approach, employing world-class people, and supporting growth in its portfolio companies and communities. KKR sponsors investment funds that invest in private equity, credit and real assets and has strategic partners that manage hedge funds. KKR’s insurance subsidiaries offer retirement, life and reinsurance products under the management of Global Atlantic Financial Group. References to KKR’s investments may include the activities of its sponsored funds and insurance subsidiaries.
TEAM OVERVIEW
The role will join the KKR Global Tax team, a world-class team of tax professionals dedicated to supporting KKR’s global investment activities. Led by the Global Head of Tax based in New York, the team encompasses experts in various areas of taxation, including transaction structuring, compliance, and strategic planning. With a global presence and a focus on collaboration, KKR Global Tax plays a pivotal role in guiding the firm’s tax strategy and ensuring compliance with tax regulations across jurisdictions. The team fosters a culture of innovation, excellence, and continuous learning, providing opportunities for professional growth and development. The U.S. Transactional Tax role will join the team as part of KKR’s continued investment in scalable transactional tax execution capabilities supporting its global private markets platform.
POSITION SUMMARY
KKR is seeking a skilled and experienced tax professional to join its Global Tax team in New York as the U.S. Transactional Tax Lead, reporting directly to the K-Series & Private Markets Head of Tax. The role will serve as the primary U.S. transactional tax execution lead for the private markets platform, with a particular focus on Infrastructure and Private Equity investments, partnering closely with deal teams throughout the transaction lifecycle to provide real-time tax support across diligence, underwriting, structuring, execution, and exit activities.
Key responsibilities include structuring U.S. transactions across KKR’s private markets platform, coordinating K-Series topside structuring for global investments, and partnering closely with regional transactional tax leads to support consistency across jurisdictions. The position will translate commercial objectives and the firm’s tax risk parameters into practical transaction structures, while coordinating closely with internal stakeholders and external tax advisors to support timely and consistent execution. The role will also support transaction-adjacent tax matters impacting portfolio investments, including restructurings, integrations, and exits.
The role requires sound transactional judgment, strong project management and communication skills, and the ability to work effectively across investment, legal, finance, compliance, and operations teams while managing multiple concurrent transactions and advisor workstreams.
RESPONSIBILITIES
Transaction Tax Execution & Structuring:
Lead U.S. transactional tax support for Infrastructure and Private Equity investments, partnering directly with deal teams throughout the transaction lifecycle.
Lead tax diligence, underwriting and structuring analyses for U.S. transactions, directing external advisors and internal workstreams to identify material tax risks, structural considerations and downstream operational implications.
Develop practical, scalable transaction structures aligned with commercial objectives and the firm’s tax risk parameters across all participating capital sources, including flagship funds, co-investment vehicles and K-Series capital.
Review and provide strategic direction on tax diligence, structuring analyses, financial models and transaction documentation prepared by external advisors, identifying key issues and driving focus toward material matters.
Review and advise on tax-related provisions in transaction documents, including purchase agreements, partnership agreements, and financing arrangements, in coordination with Legal and external counsel.
Coordinate with Legal, Finance, Compliance, Operations and external advisors to support efficient transaction execution and implementation.
K-Series Global Transaction Coordination:

Who You Are:
The Senior Mechanical Engineer, Data Center Operations Engineering & Reliability provides full-lifecycle mechanical engineering support across the data center portfolio, from site design and construction through commissioning, turnover,
and enduring operations.
This role serves as an operations-focused technical owner for mechanical infrastructure, ensuring systems are designed, built, commissioned, maintained, and operated in a way that protects uptime, preserves design intent, supports redundancy models, and improves long-term asset reliability.
The role partners with site operations, design and construction, commissioning, controls/BMS, vendors, OEMs, finance, and enterprise reliability leadership to translate design decisions and construction outcomes into safe, maintainable, and reliable operations.
What You’ll Do:
This position supports the enterprise reliability strategy, maintenance governance, asset lifecycle planning, engineering standards, RCA discipline, technical escalation model, commissioning lessons learned, and continuous improvement objectives owned by the VP, Operational Reliability & Engineering.
Key Responsibilities
1. Site Design and Pre-Construction Support
Provide mechanical engineering input during site selection, concept design, schematic design, design development, and construction document reviews.
Review mechanical design packages for operational readiness, maintainability, service access, system redundancy, capacity, resiliency, and preservation of design intent.
Evaluate mechanical system designs, including chilled water systems, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, CRAH/CRAC units, heat exchangers, economizers, valves, piping, filtration, humidification, water treatment systems, and supporting infrastructure.
Identify design risks that could create future operational issues, single points of failure, maintenance access constraints, reliability gaps, or lifecycle cost exposure.
Participate in constructability reviews, value engineering discussions, submittal reviews, RFI resolution, equipment selection reviews, and design standard updates.
Partner with design and construction teams to ensure mechanical systems align with enterprise standards, OEM requirements, warranty protections, and long-term operating expectations.
2. Construction, Commissioning, Turnover, and Operational Readiness
Support construction-phase technical reviews to ensure installed mechanical systems remain aligned with approved design intent, redundancy models, sequence requirements, and operating requirements.
Review and provide input on commissioning plans, functional performance tests, integrated systems tests, failure-mode tests, and sequence-of-operations validation.
Validate that mechanical alarms, controls sequences, set points, trends, and BMS visibility support safe and reliable operations.
Ensure turnover packages include complete O&M manuals, as-built drawings, asset data, warranty information, spare parts requirements, PM tasks, training materials, and vendor service requirements.
Confirm site operations teams are prepared to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot mechanical systems before handoff to enduring operations.
Capture construction and commissioning lessons learned and incorporate them into standards, operating procedures, maintenance programs, and future designs.
3. Enduring Operations and Reliability Engineering
Serve as a mechanical technical escalation point for site operations during incidents, abnormal operating conditions, environmental excursions, equipment failures, and reliability concerns.
Analyze mechanical system performance trends, including temperature, humidity, flow, pressure, valve position, pump performance, chiller efficiency, economizer operation, and controls stability.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Claude Code is changing how engineering organizations build software, and most of them need someone to show them how. That's you.
Technical Architects help customers get real work done with Claude Code, Claude Tag (Claude Code as an agent in Slack), and the enterprise admin controls that decide whether a rollout succeeds. You'll teach customers, partners and Anthropic's own field teams. Just as important, you'll train the trainers who carry that knowledge to everyone else.
We're hands-on AI engineers who would rather teach than sell. You'll work alongside customer engineering organizations, teaching them about Claude Code and shepherding rollouts with advanced admin knowledge. Most weeks you're in front of an audience with Claude Desktop or a terminal open: thousands of engineers on a public webinar one day, a customer's platform team in their own conference room the next week, office hours in between. The prep material often reaches you the day before.
The team is growing quickly this year, scope will grow as new products ship, and the people who join now will shape how it works.
Responsibilities
Teach in every format.
Take a standing rotation on Anthropic's public webinars in front of thousands of engineers at a time. Lead workshops and multi-day onsites, in person and virtual, built around a customer's own codebase and questions. Host office hours and multi-week cohorts where engineers, partners, and account teams bring live problems.
Teach the teachers.
Run train-the-trainer programs for customer technologists and champions, and certify them to deliver Anthropic's material.
Empower admins.
Educate enterprise admins on the technical requirements for a strong rollout by guiding them through single sign-on, permissions, connectors, spend controls, data-handling policy, and other advanced topics.
Build fast with Claude.
Turn a request into a polished deck, demo repository or plugin within a day, using the tools you teach. Explore new features the day they ship. Pick up a teammate's material and deliver it as if you wrote it.
Bring field signal back to product.
Tell the Claude Code, Claude Tag and Cowork teams what customers run into, specifically enough that they can fix it.
Be the technical voice in the room.
Partner with account executives, customer success managers, Applied AI Architects, support engineers and partner leads.
Travel.
Expect 30 to 50%, in bursts around onsites, workshops and events.
You may be a good fit if you have
5+ years as a software engineer, solutions architect, developer advocate or similar. You still ship code and regularly teach engineering audiences.
Current engineering range.
You've shipped code other people depend on. You can go deep with a senior engineer anywhere in the stack. You use Claude Code or a similar agentic tool every day and have opinions about it.
Big-stage presence.
You've held large live audiences. You sound practiced with material you got that morning, and a broken demo doesn’t faze you.
Range in one conversation.
You can go from banter to a rigorous design discussion, and both feel natural.
Care for people.
You do right by a struggling customer, and you won't leave a confused room behind.
Initiative.
You build things without waiting for permission, and you say when an idea is half-formed, including your manager's.
Steadiness
when priorities shift, timelines are short and colleagues are under pressure.
Comfort with ambiguity
in a fast-moving industry and product suite.
A stake in safe AI.
You care that large organizations deploy AI responsibly, and you want to help them do it.
You love being on the frontier.
You want to work at the edge of what’s possible and help define what comes next.

Depth in enterprise identity and security review (SAML, OIDC, SCIM, SOC 2, HIPAA).
Experience running Claude on Amazon Bedrock or Google Cloud Vertex AI.
Time with regulated industries or with systems-integrator partners.
